calibration_rulings.title: The nisba "Hasawi" (Arabic «الأحسائي») in the fruit names, all cards at once.
calibration_rulings.binds: The fifteen strings of strings_affected; every later fruit or product of Al-Ahsa that is not on the owner's list.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: every fruit name whose Arabic carries «الأحسائي» is written with the head name and the Urdu possessive — «الاحساء کا لیموں (بن زہیری)», «الاحساء کا پیلا خربوزہ», «الاحساء کا انجیر», «الاحساء کا بمبر», «الاحساء کے انگور», «الاحساء کا انار (السواری)», «الاحساء کا شہتوت», «الاحساء کا کنار (نبق)» (N282) — and in alts and running text «الاحساء کے …»; each card's number follows its source (grapes plural, the rest singular). It is what P6 rules for the lime and N115 for any adjective of Al-Ahsa, what the approved pages write for every Hasawi product (lemon-farm, home.route.s5.d, cat.taste.d, zaki-alsalem-farm), and what the Russian line did on these cards. «حساوی» stands once, inside the owner-listed name of the exhibition (N286). B is outside the owner's list; C is a coinage attested only in personal names (ur.wikipedia 41 pages, all persons). CONFIRMED on the on-05 reader: no remark on any card name of this pattern; his item 24 asks only whether «حساوی» in the exhibition is the same lime (ruled there). ROUND 2: no reader remark on the pattern itself; the on-r1 reader found the repeated «الاحساء کا …» monotonous (item 56, minor) and three names on the lime card (item 27) — ruled there; A stands.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: no Urdu adjective of Al-Ahsa on the page; «حساوی» only inside «حساوی لیموں کی نمائش».

calibration_rulings.title: The kanar card name and the gloss «بیر»: source bracket '(Nabk)' / «(النبق)» against the heading-gloss guard (P3c-labels, N103).
calibration_rulings.binds: fruits.g3.f1.name, fruits.description, fruits.heroSum; later card names only as cases of N294.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B: the card name is «الاحساء کا کنار (نبق)» — the bracket holds the second name both source names close with ('Nabk', «(النبق)»), spelled from the Arabic without the article (N284), entered as the termbase key «نبق». It is a case of N294 (fruit card names), which states the rule and why N103's 'whole title a termbase key' clause is not applied to card names. «(بیر)» (stage 1 to 5) was a gloss in a heading and is barred by P3c-labels; C («الاحساء کا بیر (کنار)») puts the head name, not the second name, in the bracket and drops 'Nabk'; D drops a name both sources carry. The help «بیر» gave stands in running text: the lead's gloss sentence («… اور کنار بیر کو۔», N291) before any card, and the description's «سدر یعنی بیری». The meta description names «کنار» bare (P3c-labels, b0-ui: a name in a snippet). COST, charged under fit: «نبق» is unknown to an Urdu reader. ROUND 2: the on-r1 reader read «(نبق)» as an unknown Arabic word and found the lead's gloss and the description work better (item 48, minor) — the help is where the ruling puts it; B stands.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: as N294; the kanar card's bracket holds «نبق»; no gloss in the meta description.
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: Judge round2, b18-ui (round 4), 2026-10-15; record corrected by the judge's addendum to that round

calibration_rulings.title: The atranj card name: English 'Atranj (Citron)' (a gloss) against Arabic «الأترنج (الأترج)» (a second name).
calibration_rulings.ruling: C (round 2; round 1's B withdrawn): the card name is «اترنج», with no bracket. N294's exception needs a second name with which BOTH source names close; here only the Arabic title does («الأترنج (الأترج)»), while the English bracket 'Citron' is a gloss — so no bracket is admitted, and a heading without one needs no exception. B «(اترج)» read as a variant spelling and stood two lines from the alt's «(ترنج)» (proof on r1, should-fix 1 and 2; on-r1 reader item 31); A «(ترنج)» is a gloss in a heading. The alt «جھری دار چھلکے والے ہرے اترنج (ترنج) کے پھل» is running text read aloud, not a heading, keeps the Urdu name of the fruit as the English alt keeps 'citron', and is the wording the on-05 reader passed. COST: the Arabic second name «الأترج» is not written on the page — logged under source_defects.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the atranj card name «اترنج» carries no bracket; its alt is not held to the heading guard.

calibration_rulings.title: Date and fruit variety names written without the Arabic article (except «السواری»).
calibration_rulings.binds: Every variety name of the page (strings_affected); every later variety or dish name that is not a place.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A with its one exception: date and fruit variety names are spelled from the Arabic WITHOUT the article («خلاص», «شیشی», «رزیز», «برحی», «بواکیر», «طیار», «مجناز», «غر», «خنیزی», «ام رحیم», «زاملی», «ہلالی», «شبیبی», «شہل», «وصیلی», «حاتمی», «کاسبی», «بن زہیری», «اترنج», «نبق», «بمبر», «کنار», «تفاحی», «ام صلیم», «صینی», «سفسیف», «جمید»), as the termbase writes dish names («ہریس», «مفلق») and the reference writes «عجوہ کھجور»; P1 binds place names. ONE EXCEPTION, «السواری», keeps the article: bare it is letter for letter the common Urdu word 'ride'. A name that reads as an Urdu word in running text takes «نامی» before its generic at its first mention in a list (N292). C refused (the homograph). CONFIRMED in part: the on-05 reader took «خلاص», «شیشی», «طیار» as words (items 9, 20) — answered by N292, not by the article; he read «السواری» as the variety's name (item 35, a source defect).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: variety names without the Arabic article, except «السواری».

calibration_rulings.title: English loans in the nutrition sentences and the Guinness name (P16 / P16-test).
calibration_rulings.binds: fruits.g0.f0.pre, fruits.g2.f0.pre, fruits.g3.f0.pre, fruits.statsSrc, fruits.g0.intro; the entries «وٹامن», «آئس کریم», «گنیز ورلڈ ریکارڈز».
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, PENDING: «وٹامن سی», «پوٹاشیم», «کیروٹینائڈز», «مینگنیز», «سیلینیم», «آئس کریم» stand as loans entered pending under P16 (no common native word for the elements, the carotenoids or ice cream as a category; «قلفی» is another sweet), as N155 entered «اسٹرابیری»; «گنیز ورلڈ ریکارڈز» is a brand in Urdu script by its reference label (P16's brand clause). P16-test (2) is NOT met for any of them (no native form was written, so no reader stumbled on one): stated, not assumed, and the entries go to the owner pending. B («حیاتین ج») refused: a lawful native word on the reference, but its «ج» for C is opaque to a lay reader and the line has no reader evidence for it. C refused: «کیروٹینائڈز» is the reference's majority form (5 to 1); N5's plural rule is for a loan the line admitted as a common noun, not a scientific name. Zinc stays the native «جست»: the reader's «زنک» (item 12) is refused under P16. ROUND 2: the on-r1 reader charged «جست» as bookish again (item 13) and the nutrient list as brochure-like (item 34): the source's content; A stands.
calibration_rulings.guard: Proofreader, checklist item 9: these loans are the batch's pending entries; any other loan in Urdu letters is reported.

calibration_rulings.title: The exhibition name «حساوی لیموں کی نمائش» in quotation marks.
calibration_rulings.binds: fruits.g1.f0.pre; any later named event the Arabic quotes and whose name carries an owner-listed nisba.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «“حساوی لیموں کی نمائش”» in quotation marks, as the Arabic quotes it. A narrow case beside N16 (5) and N113, not a general fourth use of the marks: the name of a named EVENT that the Arabic quotes and that carries the owner-listed nisba «حساوی» — the marks tell the reader that «حساوی» belongs to a name (readers of b0-ui, b9, b10 stopped at the bare nisba, N144, N154). A body still takes no marks (N16 (4)). CONFIRMED in part on the on-05 reader: he read the marks as a name and asked only whether «حساوی» means the same lime (item 24, ruled there).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: «حساوی لیموں کی نمائش» stands between U+201C and U+201D.

calibration_rulings.title: Gender of «کھجور» (date): the two normative dictionaries disagree.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «کھجور» is FEMININE, plural «کھجوریں» — Urdu Lughat «امث» (udb word=181385, HTTP 200, stage 4), the reference usage («کھجوریں» 76 pages) and the line's approved text («کھجوریں توڑنے», «ہر قسم کی کھجوریں») agree; rekhta's masculine is recorded in the entry as the dissent. The entry stays pending as stage 4 entered it (a normative source dissents). The on-05 reader read the feminine agreement without a remark (items 9, 17).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: «کھجور» agrees in the feminine.
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: Judge round2, b18-ui (round 4), 2026-10-15; record corrected by the judge's addendum to that round

calibration_rulings.title: A kept term whose first running-text mention stands inside a «سے لے کر … تک» frame (fruits.heroSum: rutab, kanar): the gloss inside the frame, between commas, or after it?
calibration_rulings.binds: fruits.heroSum; any later gloss whose first mention sits inside «سے … تک» or another framed phrase.
calibration_rulings.ruling: D (round 2, B amended by order only). gloss_regel's 'once, at the first running-text mention' is kept by a gloss in the sentence that directly follows the mention, where a gloss inside the mention's frame would split a postposition from its noun; the gloss's words are unchanged (P28: «تازہ پکی کھجوریں»; «بیر»). The frame lists the source's three fruits with the lime beside the summer rutab, so that no reader takes the lime for a winter fruit (two readers of two did); nothing enters or leaves.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: no «یعنی» gloss between «سے لے کر» and «تک».

calibration_rulings.title: Variety names that read as common Urdu words («خلاص», «شیشی», «طیار») in a running-text list.
calibration_rulings.binds: fruits.g0.intro, fruits.g0.f4.pre; any later list of variety names that read as Urdu words.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: in RUNNING TEXT, a list of variety names whose first names read as Urdu words carries «نامی» and a generic after its first names, once: «خلاص، شیشی اور رزیز نامی اقسام» (g0.intro), «طیار، مجناز اور غر نامی کھجوریں» (g0.f4.pre; round 2: «کھجوریں», not «اقسام», which stood four times in the card — proof on r1, should-fix 3). Later names of the same list stand bare under it. Alt texts and headings are outside the ruling. B refused (N16 (5), N113: the sources quote none of these names); C leaves the misreading. CONFIRMED by the on-r1 reader (item 24: «نامی» helps).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: in a description or intro, the first running-text list of date varieties whose names read as Urdu words has «نامی» and a generic after its first names; alt texts and headings are outside the guard.

calibration_rulings.title: The Bawakir card name: EN 'Bawakir — early & local varieties' (a dash gloss), AR «البواكير والأصناف المحلية» (two things).
calibration_rulings.binds: fruits.g0.f4.name (also the first cell of its row in the seasons table).
calibration_rulings.ruling: B: the English's 'early' as the attribute of the name, then the Arabic's 'and the local varieties'; no comma, no bracket, no gloss device in the heading (P3c-labels). C refused: a bracket in a heading, and «دوسری» is not in the source. The name «بواکیر» is spelled from the Arabic without the article (N284). ROUND 2: the on-r1 reader found «بواکیر» unexplained and 'early-ripening Bawakir' redundant once he guessed its meaning (item 22, moderate); the stage-5 heading was contested by both earlier readers, so B stands, charged under fit.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the Bawakir heading carries no comma and no bracket.

calibration_rulings.title: Fruit card names (interface headings h4, also the first cell of the seasons table) with a source bracket: under P3c-labels and N103, which bracket may they keep, and does N103's clause 'the whole title a termbase key' apply?
calibration_rulings.binds: The card names fruits.g1.f0.name, fruits.g2.f4.name and fruits.g3.f1.name (a bracket each) and fruits.g1.f1.name (no bracket, N283 C); every later fruit or product CARD NAME whose source names close with a bracket. Not other interface headings, labels or section titles: they stay under N103's one case.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. A fruit card name keeps the second name both source names close with, in one closing bracket, as that name's termbase key and nothing else; N103's purpose — the bracket holds a registered NAME, never a gloss — is met by the bracketed name being a key. The clause 'the whole title a termbase key' binds page titles and is not applied to card names, which are not keys (B would enter fifteen phrases of N281 as names). No gloss, no Urdu name of the fruit and no generic in a card-name bracket (P3c-labels); a source bracket that holds a gloss on either side gives no bracket (N283 C). C refused: it drops names both sources carry. THIS RULING AMENDS THE GUARD OF P3c-labels, as N103 amended it in b7: the guard's 'the one case of item N103' becomes two cases, the second being this one, written into the guard's text (addendum to judge round 2, base_amendments), so that the ruling, its guard and the base guard agree and stand alone. COST, charged: «بن زہیری» (four readers) and «نبق» (two) are unknown words to the reader; neither source explains them.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a fruit card name closes with at most one bracket; the bracket holds a termbase key that both source names carry in their closing bracket, and nothing else; P3c-labels' guard carries this as its second case (item N294).
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: Judge round2, b18-ui (round 4), 2026-10-15; record corrected by the judge's addendum to that round

calibration_rulings.title: A name of this kind where no gloss is possible (a title, a label, a list, a snippet).
calibration_rulings.binds: Titles, labels and questions of both attraction batches. LEFT TO b2: nothing; its five titles stand bare. ‖ b7, ROUND 2: kanzan-park::title, under the exception of item N103.
calibration_rulings.ruling: As b0-ui ruled it: in a label, a list, a title and a meta description the name stands bare, byte-identical to its termbase key; the plain Urdu generic may stand in the neighbouring line and never touches the name. Not reopened. In running text point (2) of P3c applies. b2, ROUND 3: adopted as it stands; b2's five titles and ten labels are bare. ‖ AMENDED IN b7, ROUND 2 (item N103), in its guard only: 'no bracket in a title' now names its one exception, the second name of kanzan-park's title, which both source titles carry in a closing bracket and which is a name, not a gloss. A gloss, an Urdu generic or any other word in a bracket stays barred in a title, a kicker, a label and a question. The stage checker's heading probe was taught the same exception by the coordinator.
calibration_rulings.guard: As b0-ui's: no bracket in a title, kicker, label or question, save the one case of item N103 of b7 — a title that closes with a single bracket pair holding a second name with which BOTH source titles close in a bracket, the whole title being a termbase key byte for byte, and the second case of item N294 of b18-ui — a fruit card name (an interface heading, not a page title) that closes with a single bracket pair holding a second name with which BOTH source names close in a bracket, that second name being a termbase key byte for byte and nothing else standing in the bracket (the whole card name is not a key); no Urdu generic next to a name that already carries its Arabic generic (a generic after «نامی», in running text, is not next to the name).
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: Round 1 judge, b0-ui round 3; confirmed and extended by b2 round 3, 2026-10-12; guard amended by the b7 judge, round 2, 2026-10-14
